problem: Given that $Q(1,3,5)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨-4,1,-3⟩=-16$, find the shortest distance from $P(-3,7,3)$ to $Π.$
worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,3,5⟩-⟨-3,7,3⟩ \\  & =⟨4,-4,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-4,1,-3⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|4\cdot (-4)+(-4)\cdot 1+2\cdot (-3)|}{\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-16-4-6|}{\sqrt{16+1+9}} \\  & =\frac{|-26|}{\sqrt{26}} \\  & =\sqrt{26}\end{aligned}
$$
